working_title: Inside Wedillybird 4: planners, one calm status per couple
search_intent: wedding planner software to track guest lists

hook.spoken: Planners, your guest tracker belongs on a dashboard, not a group chat.
hook.visual: NORAH L7-S5 stopping inside a glass orangery with long bare tables; overlay = hook

voiceover: Planners, your guest tracker belongs on a dashboard, not a group chat. One calm status per couple, from one screen. Stay for the three-line status you can send every couple. Every wedding you run gets its own group chat. Every chat asks the same question: who's coming, and who isn't? So you become the dashboard, updating counts by hand. And your leads sit in notes and direct messages. Then a couple asks where things stand, and you open three apps. This is the planner cockpit in Wedillybird, built for several weddings at once. It lists your upcoming weddings, each with its RSVP progress. And an activity feed shows what changed lately. Open it before a client call, and each wedding's status is right there. Here's the part people skip: your leads. That's the CRM, a kanban board for new inquiries. Lead, Contacted, Quote, Booked, In progress, Delivered. Move a lead across as the conversation moves. Add notes to a card, so the context travels with it. When a lead books, turn it into a wedding. If you're a planner, follow. Tomorrow evening: entry nine of Norah's Notebook. One thing to know: Wedillybird's CRM isn't on every plan. The kanban board comes with the higher plans, not the entry one. Here's the three-line status I promised. Replies in. Still waiting on. Next decision. Send the same three lines every time. The first two lines are your RSVP progress, in words. Short on purpose, so it's easy to send and easy to read. One cockpit, one board, one calm status per couple. See a sample invitation: link in bio. I'm Norah, Wedillybird's AI host. So, planners: where does your guest tracker live today?

caption:
Wedding planner software: a guest tracker that isn't a group chat.
A look at the planner cockpit and the CRM kanban board, plus a three-line status you can send every couple. The CRM comes with the higher plans.
Hosted by Norah, an AI character created by the Wedillybird team.
pinned_comment: The three-line status to send every couple: 1) Replies in. 2) Still waiting on. 3) Next decision. Same three lines, every time. The planner cockpit lists your weddings with their RSVP progress; the CRM kanban board (Lead, Contacted, Quote, Booked, In progress, Delivered) comes with the higher plans. Norah is AI-generated. Screens shown are real Wedillybird screens (demo data).
comment_bait: Planners: where does your guest tracker live today?

needs_proof: S11 capture: the cockpit lists upcoming weddings with RSVP progress and an activity feed (r3 B4, convex/pro.ts, components/pro/cockpit.tsx). Crop or blur quota gauges, plan names and prices so nothing on screen contradicts 'no plan names, quotas or prices'.

S12 capture: six columns Lead, Contacted, Quote, Booked, In progress, Delivered; notes; lead-to-wedding conversion (r3 B4, convex/clients.ts). Confirm the 'turn it into a wedding' control is visible in the capture, otherwise the card fallback carries it.
Tier statement: the CRM kanban is Business and up (lib/payments/entitlements.ts:108-117) and is voiced only as 'the higher plans', with no plan name.
Do not open the agency wedding-hub tabs (messaging, check-in, gallery are simulated); only the cockpit and the CRM are shown.
claims_review.notes: No r2 facts and no figures: the three-line status is Norah's suggestion, not a sourced practice, and 'three apps' is illustrative. No plan names, quotas or prices. 'Higher plans' is the honest limit. Wedillybird is named three times (beats 9, 20, 28). The hook is written in the H26/H27 style (the calendar lists H26).
